//: AI provider profiles. AI_PROVIDER (config/service.json or the environment) names one of these, or `mock` for the sample data in src/mocks. Each profile says which implementation answers (`kind`: one file in src/providers/text), which environment variable holds its key (`keyEnv`; the key itself goes in .env or the secret store, never here), the model and thinking level per tier, and the list prices used to show cost. Switching provider is a change of AI_PROVIDER plus the key; no code change. Override the location with AI_PROVIDERS_CONFIG_PATH.
//tiers: Spec section 9: the complex tier runs research, roles, competencies and the review checklist; the default tier runs activities and ladders. `thinking` is low | medium | high per tier and is mapped to each API's own setting (Claude effort, Gemini thinkingLevel).
//free: `freeTier: true` means calls are not billed. The cost shown is then what the same tokens would cost at the listed paid prices, marked as an estimate. `maxConcurrent` caps calls in flight across all jobs, to stay under a low requests-per-minute quota; leave it out to use the batch settings only.

gemini-free.//: Gemini API free tier (checked 6 Nov 2026): gemini-3.8-flash is free; gemini-4-argon and Google Search grounding are not, so research runs without web search. Prices are the paid-tier list prices for gemini-3.8-flash, used only for the estimate.

gemini-paid.//: Gemini API paid tier (prices checked 6 Nov 2026; gemini-4-argon prices are due to rise on 1 Dec 2026). Google Search is billed per search query after 5,000 free a month; Gemini cannot limit search to named domains, so the research prompt asks for them instead.

claude.//: Claude Sonnet 5.5 on both tiers (team decision, 4 Nov 2026; the spec suggests Opus for complex). Prices checked 4 Nov 2026. Cache writes bill at 1.25x input.
